analysis:
The PR adds a 30s startup-discovery retry to the root fan helper (TB-010; relevant threats T-046, T-047, T-048). The changed code is FanDaemon.swift: recoverStartupInventory (head 250-298), lifecycleRevision, shuttingDown, pendingRestorations, and an injectable thermalState. The docs and changelog describe the same behavior.

Safety properties I checked in the head text:
- Recovery requires effectiveEnabled, no power suspension, and an unchanged lifecycleRevision (head 300-302). emergencyRestore, shutdown, prepareForSleep and didWake each bump the revision, so a stale discovery cannot revive a disabled or sleeping helper.
- Replacement of the inventory and controller happens only when hasPossibleOwnership is false and pendingRestorations==0 (head 278-286). The swap has no suspension point.
- The swap clears providerLease and policy samples, so a fresh lease is needed before engaging. Discovery itself never writes to the SMC.
- tick returns early while a restoration is pending or the helper is shutting down (head 205). Shutdown performs its own restore.
- The lease-renewal path is unchanged. A lease renewed while the inventory is unusable is discarded at the swap.

Residual uncertainty for the next pass:
- FanOwnershipRecovery.reconcile (not supplied) runs with the unusable inventory at head 260 and 369. If the journal lists fan indices or Ftst that the empty inventory cannot address, the journal might be deleted (head 377) while hardware stays in manual mode. Later discovery would then not restore it. This needs verification in FanOwnershipRecovery.swift.
- The new test harness (f712a72149b38034) was provided as metadata only, so test coverage of these races was not reviewed.
- The retry runs as root every 30s against the SMC, so confirm that reader.discover is read-only.

No new trust-boundary or XPC authentication changes. No coordinator, provider-attestation or encryption interactions are touched.
